dialogue.line: Oh, my notebook’s in black and white.
Aurora never told me why. I guess it’s an aesthetic choice.
(It doesn't take you a second to realize who's speaking. That's the first time you hear her voice beyond your textual exchange. Her voice is huskier than you thought.)
Aurora? Is that you? The connection’s finally back. I’ve landed safely on Twins.
Glad you’re safe! I hope the trip wasn’t too rough. Have you had a chance to look through your handbook?
Yeah, I was just looking at it. Interesting color scheme.

There’s a reason for it. Seen from space, Twins is a planet in black and white... Just like the civilization that once lived there. Of course, that's a bonus to that name. When it was first named as the Twins, it's because it has an aligned Day and Night with the Earth, despite the distance between.
Should I expect to meet anyone here?

No, but you’ll find their traces—a fallen civilization of two cities. Our archaeologists have searched their libraries, their homes, their schools. All the places where they lived. But there’s one place they overlooked.
(You might have an answer in mind. But you wait for her confirmation.)
Where they remembered the dead. The cemeteries. That’s your mission: to uncover what words alone cannot tell us, through the memories they left behind.
We don’t have much transmission time left. I have to go. Talk to you later.
(Now it’s just you, your handbook, and the faint breath of the planet.)
(You feel a tremor in your limbs.)
(You stand up. The faint breeze brushing past your ears feels much like the wind back home. Perhaps the people who once lived here weren’t so different from you, either.)
(You’re here to gather their memories. Your steps grow steadier.)
(Then you see it: the place where an entire civilization rests.)
